rules.statement: "Are you sure?" modal vs undo toast

check.look_for:
PASS if a truly unrecoverable, high-cost destructive action (delete account, permanent
data loss) is gated behind a confirmation dialog.
PASS if a cheap, frequent, server-side-reversible destructive action (archive, remove a
tag, delete a row) executes immediately with an undo toast (roughly 4-8s window).
FLAG if a low-stakes, frequent action is gated behind a blocking confirm dialog, or if
a truly unrecoverable action relies only on an undo toast.
NOT-APPLICABLE if there is no destructive action in the bundle, or reversibility
cannot be determined from the bundle.

evidence.name: Nielsen Norman Group and similar usability-research firms — confirmation-dialog and undo-pattern guidance
evidence.incentive: paid usability consultancies; findings come from their own studies, not an independent meta-analysis

rules.statement: Inline per-field errors vs a summary banner

check.look_for:
PASS if a form of roughly 6 or fewer fields shows errors inline, next to each failing
field, on submit.
PASS if a longer or multi-section form shows a summary banner above the form on
submit, with each item deep-linking to its field, in addition to (or instead of)
inline text.
FLAG if a long form relies on inline-only errors with nothing surfaced above the fold
on submit, or if a 1-2 field form shows a summary banner that duplicates
already-visible inline text.
NOT-APPLICABLE if the form has no validation, or error placement cannot be determined
from the bundle.

rules.statement: Artificial head-start progress vs honest, zero-start progress indicators

check.look_for: Pre-filling a progress bar to show a head start leverages a real, well-studied motivation effect; faking progress the user didn't earn is a manipulation some teams and users will not accept once they notice.

evidence.name: Goal-gradient hypothesis — Hull (1932, 1934); Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng, "The Goal-Gradient Hypothesis Resurrected: Purchase Acceleration, Illusionary Goal Progress, and Customer Retention" (University of Chicago); as curated on lawsofux.com
evidence.incentive: the underlying psychology (people work harder as perceived proximity to a goal increases) is genuine, peer-reviewed research with no commercial stake in this specific application; lawsofux.com's own citation quality varies entry to entry

evidence.name: Applied "pre-fill for a psychological head start" recommendation, as framed by this corpus
evidence.incentive: this specific application — artificially crediting progress the user hasn't made — is a growth/engagement tactic, not part of the cited research itself, and is the actual point of contention here

stance.why: waste of space

rules.statement: Autofocus the first field vs leaving initial focus untouched

check.look_for: Autofocusing the primary input on a dedicated data-entry screen removes a click; autofocusing on a content page or on mobile can jar a reader, jump scroll position, or trigger the keyboard unexpectedly.

evidence.name: GoodUI pattern library (goodui.org), "Auto Focused Form Field" — pattern name only
evidence.incentive: conversion-rate optimization vendor; the source scrape captured the pattern's title but no experiment description or measured result for this one

evidence.name: WAI unexpected-change-of-context guidance (WCAG 3.2.1/3.2.2 territory)
evidence.incentive: standards-adjacent concern, no commercial stake — autofocus stealing focus on page load is a documented failure pattern (WCAG technique F41) when it moves a screen-reader user's position without warning

stance.why: better user experience for keyboard user

rules.statement: Ruthless field elimination vs fields kept for a real downstream reason

check.look_for: Removing every non-essential field raises completion; some "non-essential" fields exist for fraud prevention, account recovery, or a genuine later need, and removing them just defers the ask.

evidence.name: GoodUI pattern library (goodui.org), "Fewer Form Fields" — a real cited test (password/email confirmation removed from a signup/checkout funnel, replaced with an auto-generated password emailed to the user; impact on progression and sales measured)
evidence.incentive: conversion-rate optimization vendor — the cited metric is completion/sales, not data quality, account-recovery cost, or fraud risk; a field's removal can look purely like a win when measured only on the funnel it was cut from

rules.statement: Conversational (mad-libs) form inputs vs traditional stacked forms

check.look_for: Embedding inputs into a readable sentence can feel less clinical for a short filter or intake question; it gets awkward and hard to scan once the data being collected is long or structurally complex.

evidence.name: GoodUI pattern library (goodui.org), "Natural Language Forms" — pattern name only

rules.statement: Reveal form fields incrementally vs showing the whole form upfront

check.look_for: Starting with only the most critical fields and revealing the rest as the user commits lowers perceived length; showing everything upfront lets a user judge full scope and trust before investing any effort.

evidence.name: GoodUI pattern library (goodui.org), "Progressive Fields" — a real cited test (a buy-box component initially shown with fewer, smaller fields; impact on initial progression and sales measured). The source notes the experiment ran shorter than usual after triggering a loss-protection stop rule, so the vendor's own writeup flags the effect may be inflated from lower statistical power.
evidence.incentive: conversion-rate optimization vendor, and this specific result is explicitly flagged by the source as possibly underpowered

check.look_for: A persistent, wide search input maximizes usage on content- or catalog-heavy sites; collapsing it behind an icon reclaims header space for guided browsing on marketing or portfolio sites.

rules.statement: Skeleton screens vs spinners

check.look_for:
PASS if list/card content with a known, fixed layout shows gray placeholder blocks
matching that layout while loading.
PASS if content of genuinely unpredictable shape, or a wait under roughly 1 second,
shows a plain spinner instead.
FLAG if a fixed-layout list/card view shows only a bare spinner for a wait over a
couple of seconds, or if a skeleton is built for content whose shape varies too much
for the skeleton to resemble the result.
NOT-APPLICABLE if there is no loading state to observe, or wait duration/layout
predictability cannot be determined from the bundle.

evidence.name: Doherty Threshold — Doherty & Thadani, "The Economic Value of a Rapid Response Time", IBM Systems Journal, 1982; as curated on lawsofux.com
evidence.incentive: original study is vendor-neutral (IBM research on system response time); lawsofux.com's curation is a psychology reference whose citation quality varies entry to entry

rules.statement: What simulated users can and cannot stand in for

check.look_for: Persona agents supplement research, never replace it; LLMs misportray and flatten identity groups, worst where identity matters.

evidence.name: Angelina Wang, Jamie Morgenstern and John P. Dickerson, "Large language models that replace human participants can harmfully misportray and flatten identity groups", Nature Machine Intelligence
evidence.incentive: academic researchers; no product interest stated

rules.statement: Space is the deciding variable: an element keeps its space only by earning it

check.look_for:
PASS if every element occupying significant space on the screen is carrying its weight — conveying information, offering an action, or giving structure a reader needs.
FLAG if something takes real space without earning it: progress credited before the user did anything, a tooltip or panel dumping fields beyond what the hover implied, decorative filler standing in for an empty state, or form fields with no stated downstream purpose.
Density itself is NOT a finding. A dense screen where every element earns its place passes; a sparse screen carrying one unearned ornament flags. Do not reward minimalism as such.
NOT-APPLICABLE if the screen has no substantive content to weigh, or the screenshot is unavailable.

evidence.name: Rex's own recorded picks and rationales in knowledge/taste/.picks/ — six entries across onboarding, forms, dataviz, empty and nav
evidence.incentive: none external; this is the substrate reading Rex back to himself, which is self-referential by construction. Its worth depends entirely on whether he recognises the pattern as his — that is what confirmation is for.

stance.why:
Confirmed 2026-08-01. The reasoning is the six calls this was read out of, in my own words at the time:

- prefilled progress bar: "waste of space"
- progressive reveal: "better space utilization"
- tooltip: "depends on the platform, but overall shorter the better"
- top-aligned labels: "much better for this case due to long field"
- empty state: "it really depends on the space and the design"
- visible search bar: "also depends on the spaces"

And the two that stop this being a minimise-everything rule, also mine:

- justified fields: "they all still need to be seen. if unnecessayr they shouldnt be seen here."
- visible search bar over a hidden icon — more permanent chrome, kept because it earns it.

rules.statement: How much to put in a chart tooltip

check.look_for: A minimal tooltip (exact value plus 2-3 supporting fields) answers what the hover implies; a denser tooltip serves power users who want more context without opening the underlying table — a real density/clarity tradeoff.

evidence.incentive: none identifiable — this is a design convention, not a cited finding; treat the specific "2-3 fields" figure as a reasonable-sounding heuristic, not a measured threshold

rules.statement: Validate on blur, not on submit

check.look_for:
PASS if field-level errors appear after a field loses focus and only for fields the
user has already interacted with.
FLAG if all errors appear only on submit attempt, or if errors appear on every
keystroke before the field has ever been blurred, or if an untouched field is
pre-marked as invalid on load.
NOT-APPLICABLE if no form has 3 or more fields, or if validation behavior cannot be
determined from the bundle (say which).

stance.why:
Errors should land next to the mistake while I still remember making it. A submit-time
wall makes me re-read a form I already thought I was done with. I accept that the
evidence for this is weak and vendor-tinted — this is a call, not a finding.
